user.title: Battery
user.description: Describe your storage. Nameplate capacity can be left as the manufacturer's figure — if a BMS reports the real (degraded) capacity, point the capacity sensor at it and that will be used instead.

data.derate_capacity_by_soh: Scale nameplate capacity by reported health
data.battery_min_soc: Minimum state of charge the optimiser may plan to
data.battery_reserve_soc: Emergency reserve written to the inverter
data.derive_wear_from_cost: Work the wear allowance out from the pack cost
data.battery_residual_value: Residual value at end of life

data_description.battery_soc_entity: Leave empty to use the inverter's own reading. A separate BMS figure is usually more accurate.
data_description.battery_min_soc: The floor for planning. The emergency reserve sits below this.
data_description.cycle_cost_per_kwh: Ignored when the allowance is being derived from cost. Watch the 'Wear allowance in use' sensor to see which figure is in force.
data_description.derive_wear_from_cost: On: the allowance is (cost − residual) ÷ (cycles × usable kWh). Off: the wear allowance below is used as entered.
data_description.battery_expected_cycles: Equivalent full cycles over the SoC window you configured above — not the headline figure quoted at a shallower depth of discharge. 1000–2000 is realistic for a used EV pack worked hard.
data_description.battery_residual_value: Leave at zero for a salvage pack.

inverter.title: Inverter
inverter.description:
Control is applied through your existing inverter integration's entities.

Auto-discovered so far: {discovered}

data.manage_export_limit: Also manage the inverter's export limit

data_description.inverter_entity_prefix: Used to pick the right entities if you have more than one inverter, e.g. "solax".
data_description.nominal_voltage: Used to convert a power target into a battery current limit when the inverter limits by current. The live voltage sensor is preferred when available.
data_description.grid_export_limit_kw: Your permitted export, e.g. 3.68 kW for a typical single-phase G98 connection.

tariff.title: Tariff sources
tariff.description: Choose where prices come from. Import prices are required; an export tariff is optional — leave it as "none" if you are not paid for export.

tariff_import.title: Import tariff
tariff_import.description: Prices are normalised to pence per kWh. If your source publishes pounds, that is detected automatically.

data_description.import_rate_entity: Entities carrying a list of forward rates, such as the Octopus Energy integration's rate events.
data_description.octopus_account: Supply this with an API key and the tariff codes will be looked up for you.
data_description.import_fixed_rate: Used as a fallback if the chosen source returns no prices.

forecast.title: Forecasting
forecast.description: A solar forecast integration is optional. With one, its shape is trusted and a per-installation correction is learned; without one, generation is learned from your own history.

data_description.solar_forecast_entities: Solcast or Forecast.Solar sensors. Add both today and tomorrow to cover the whole horizon.
data_description.weather_entity: Supplies cloud cover for solar and temperature for heating and cooling load.
data_description.load_power_entity: Needed for the load model to learn. Without it, forecasts stay on the default profile.
data_description.default_daily_load_kwh: Only used for slots not yet learned.

optimiser.title: Optimiser
optimiser.description: Inverter control starts switched off, so you can watch the plan for a few days before letting it act. Arm it later with the "Inverter control" switch.

data.terminal_value_mode: Value of energy left at the end of the horizon

data_description.horizon_hours: Longer sees further ahead but relies more on extrapolated prices.
data_description.soc_levels: Higher is more precise and slightly slower. 60 is plenty for a domestic battery.
data_description.terminal_value_mode: Stops the optimiser dumping the battery into the final slot just because the horizon ends there.
data_description.dry_run: Strongly recommended for a new install.
data_description.log_retention_days: How many days of half-hourly history to record for the 'Export performance history' action. Roughly 48 rows per day; set to 0 to keep none.

sessions.title: Grid incentive sessions
sessions.description: Octopus Saving Sessions pay you per kWh of reduction against your usual usage, and Power Up sessions make import free for a window. Point these at the Octopus Energy integration's session entities and the planner will reprice those windows automatically.

data.only_joined_sessions: Only act on sessions you have joined

data_description.saving_session_entities: The events or binary sensors carrying session windows, e.g. the Octopus Energy integration's Octoplus saving session entities.
data_description.saving_session_rate: Used only when the supplier does not publish a rate for the session. Historic Demand Flexibility rates have been well above 100p/kWh.
data_description.only_joined_sessions: Strongly recommended. Discharging hard for a session you have not opted into earns nothing.

outage.title: Power cut anticipation
outage.description: Holds extra charge back when a power cut looks likely. This can only raise the planning floor, never lower it. Check the Outage risk sensor's max_wind attribute to pick thresholds that suit your location and the units your weather entity reports.

data.outage_reserve_soc: Reserve to hold when risk is elevated
data.outage_high_reserve_soc: Reserve to hold when risk is high

data_description.outage_risk_entity: Any binary sensor: a weather warning integration, a DNO scraper, or a manual toggle.
data_description.outage_wind_threshold: In whatever unit your weather entity reports gusts in, typically km/h. Leave at 0 to ignore wind.

shifting.title: Flexible loads
shifting.description:
Loads whose timing can move. These are scheduled into the cheapest windows and the battery re-plans around them.

No smart appliances needed: leave the switch entity off a load and it is scheduled and published as advice, which you read off the 'Scheduled flexible loads' sensor and act on yourself. Give a load a switch entity and it can be driven automatically instead.

data_description.shiftable_loads: One per line: Dishwasher=1.2kWh@2kW,22:00-06:00 -- name, energy, power and the local window it must run inside. Add a third field to have it switched for you, e.g. Immersion=3kWh@3kW,00:00-07:00,switch.immersion.
data_description.appliance_control: Only affects loads you gave a switch entity. It switches them on at the start of their window and off at the end, and never touches anything you started yourself.

recommend.title: Tariff comparison
recommend.description: Compares tariffs by running the optimiser on your own learned profile, so the ranking reflects what your battery can actually exploit. Run it from the 'Compare tariffs' button.

data_description.recommend_import_products: Comma separated Octopus product codes. Leave empty for a sensible default set.
data_description.recommend_window_hours: Agile publishes only 24-48 hours ahead, so a longer window is not necessarily better.

error.octopus_unreachable: Could not reach the Octopus API. Check your network and try again.
error.octopus_no_rates: That tariff returned no rates. Check the product code and region.
error.octopus_tariff_required: Provide either a full tariff code, or a product code plus region, or an account number and API key.
error.octopus_account_failed: Could not read that Octopus account. Check the account number and API key.

export_performance.name: Export performance history
export_performance.description: Return the recorded half-hourly history and the metrics computed from it: actual spend against what no battery and a self-use battery would have cost, solar and load forecast error, plan fidelity and measured round-trip efficiency. Optionally writes a CSV under the config directory.

days.description: How much history to include, measured back from the newest record.

format.name: Format
format.description: Summary returns the metrics only. Slots adds every half-hour as structured data. CSV adds the same rows as text you can copy out whole.

write_file.name: Write a CSV file
write_file.description: Also write the rows to config/ess_controller/performance_<entry>.csv and return the path.
